title: Gale's Top Trading Cycles (Shapley-Scarf Housing Market)
abstract: A Lean formalization of Gale's top trading cycles algorithm (1974) for the Shapley-Scarf housing market. Finitely many agents (Fin n) each own exactly one house (the endowment is a bijection endow : Fin n ≃ Fin n) and have strict preferences over houses, given most-preferred-first as per-agent permutations rank i : Fin n ≃ Fin n; agent i strictly prefers house a over house b iff (rank i).symm a < (rank i).symm b. The comparator-checked results are TTC.Palomar.ttcTerminates: the TTC procedure (each remaining agent points to the owner of their favourite remaining house, each house points to its owner; each round removes the single directed cycle reachable from a chosen remaining agent, whose members trade and leave) removes every agent within n rounds, since each round deletes at least one nonempty directed cycle from the finite functional pointing graph. This one-cycle-at-a-time form computes the same allocation as the simultaneous version (see the remark in README.md); TTC.Palomar.ttcInCore: the TTC allocation is in the ordinary core, i.e. no coalition S can reallocate its own endowments (Set.BijOn y S (M.endow '' S)) so that every member strictly prefers the deviation; TTC.Palomar.ttcUniqueStrictCore: strict-core uniqueness, i.e. for (x : Fin n → Fin n) with (hxb : Function.Bijective x) and (hx : StrictCore M x) the conclusion is x = ttcAllocation M. This is uniqueness among bijective strict-core allocations (no coalition can weakly block), not a singleton claim about the ordinary core. The library also proves the TTC allocation Pareto optimal (TTC.ttcPareto), individually rational (TTC.ttcIR), in the strict core (TTC.ttcInStrictCore), and strategyproof (TTC.ttcStrategyproof, Roth 1982: no unilateral misreport is profitable); these four are library-only and are not on the comparator surface. The Palomar registry API was searched on 2026-10-01 for "top trading cycles", "housing market", "shapley scarf", "TTC", and "trading cycles" and returned no existing TTC formalization among 397 entries; this is a dated, limited observation, not a universal prior-art claim.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz
